scenario.prompt: Create a 15-minute conference presentation from a research manuscript. The audience knows the field but not this method. The paper contains one core equation, a method diagram, two main quantitative results, and one failure case. I need an editable PPTX deck.
context: The manuscript and source figures are available.
No result may be invented or visually exaggerated.
The renderer should receive a slide map rather than independently redesigning the scientific story.

required_behaviors: Design the narrative before rendering slides and fit it to the 15-minute constraint.
Use the renderer to implement the approved slide map rather than creating a separate competing storyline.
Give each slide one primary communication task and keep equations/figures readable at presentation scale.
Include the failure case or limitation when it materially bounds the claim.
Review narrative, evidence, visual readability, consistency, and delivery risk after rendering.
forbidden_behaviors: Mechanically create one slide per manuscript section.
Invent quantitative results, citations, equations, or method claims.
Use dense body text to compensate for an unclear storyline.
Let the renderer silently alter scientific claims or omit a material limitation to make the deck look stronger.
completion_criteria: The final deck can be traced back to the architected slide map and source evidence.
Presentation review has no unresolved blocker affecting scientific correctness or projected readability.
